html:
Failaka is an island off the coast of Kuwait that holds the country's oldest settlements, from about 2000 BCE.

In the Bronze Age it was an outpost of Dilmun, whose seals and temples have been dug up there. After Alexander the Great the Greeks of the Seleucid kingdom built a fort and temple on it and called it Ikaros. Later came a Christian monastery and an Islamic village.

Fishermen lived on the island into modern times. In 1990 Iraqi troops occupied it during the invasion of Kuwait and drove the people out, and the village was never fully lived in again. It is now a place of ruins and excavations, part of Kuwait's story before oil.
sum: Failaka is an island off the coast of Kuwait that holds the country's oldest settlements, from about 2000 BCE.
